In order to be eligible, organizations must have a DUNS number, a, link, SAM dot gov, account, a, link, Grants dot gov,

heading, level 2, Eligible Service Areas
In order to be eligible for R 3 grant funding, the activities proposed in a submitted grant
application must be focused on a designated R 3 area (the shaded areas in the map below). This means
that an organization’s service area under the R 3 NOFO must include one or more R 3 areas.
Organizations applying for funding do not need to be located within these R 3 areas, but
applications will be given priority if they are submitted by organizations within these R 3 areas,
if they are on behalf of collaboratives that contain such organizations, or if the majority of
their employees live within R 3 areas.
heading, level 2, Using the R 3 Map to Determine Eligibility and Funding Level
To find out if an address is located in an R 3 area, or to get information on an R 3 area for
application purposes, enter the address into the search bar (top right) or zoom in ( plus ) on the
address on the map. Any address appearing in a color-coded, shaded area is within an R 3 area. Click
the shaded area to see its R 3 Area ID and funding information needed for the grant application's
Program Narrative.

out of caption, out of figure, heading, level 2, 1. Locate Areas
R 3 funds are awarded regionally and based on population size to ensure grant equity across
Illinois. There are 12 total R 3 funding regions, which are composed of Illinois counties.
Applicants may provide services across multiple regions but must submit applications for each
specific region they intend to serve. The eligibility map above depicts the boundaries of each
service region and you may select your region in step 1. If you are unsure what funding region your
services fall under, skip to step 2 and search your address using the search tool and zoom out to
determine your region.

heading, level 2, Analysis
R 3 areas were identified via an analysis of community-level data on gun injury, child poverty,
unemployment, and state prison commitments and returns, combined with Disproportionately Impacted
Areas identified by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO). This
document outlines the criteria and data sources used to define R 3 areas, analyzed by census tract
in Illinois. Identified R 3 areas were required to meet all criteria listed in Part I or Part 2.
heading, level 3, Part I Criteria
heading, level 4, 1. Highest rates of gun injury
Cutoff, : Gun injury hospitalization rate of greater 2.7 per 10,000 residents or gun injury death rate of greater
0.49 per 10,000 residents
Data, : Hospital discharge records and vital records death records; records limited to
assault-related gun injury and assault-related gun death records
Source, : Illinois Department of Public Health
Time Period, : 2018-2022
heading, level 4, 2. Highest rates of unemployment
Cutoff, : Greater than 7.1 percent unemployment rate or less than 77.2 percent labor force participation rate
Source, : 5-year American Community Survey
Time Period, : 2017-2021
heading, level 4, 3. Highest child poverty rates
Cutoff, : Greater than 48.9 percent of children under six years-old living at or below 200 percent of the federal
poverty line
Source, : 5-year American Community Survey
Time Period, : 2017-2021
heading, level 4, 4. Highest rates of commitments to and returns from the Illinois Department of Corrections
Cutoff, : Greater than 57.9 prison commitments per 10,000 residents or greater than 53.8 prison
returns per 10,000 residents
Data, : Criminal History Record Information (CHRI); Prison and Mandatory Supervised Release (MSR)
stock files
Sources, : Illinois State Police; Illinois Department of Corrections
Time Periods, : 2018-2022
heading, level 3, Part II Criterion
heading, level 4, 1. High need, underserved, disproportionately impacted by historical economic disinvestment
Cutoff, : Defined as a Disproportionately Impacted Area
Source, : Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO) analysis
